result.text: First, the implements are prepared, the hands are washed, and the doctor gets in sterile clothes.
The doctor cleans the puncture area, and drapes the puncture zone.
The doctor configures the ultrasound, and puts gel in the probe.
Then, the doctor covers the probe and puts the sterile gel.
The doctor positions the probe and positions the patient.
The vein is identified using an anatomic identification, a doppler identification, or a compression identification.
The patient is anesthetize and punctured.
The blood return is checked.
If the blood return is not correct, the doctor goes back to the puncture step.
If the blood return is correct, the probe is dropped and the syringe is removed.
The guidewire is installed, and the trocar is removed.
Then the wire is checked using a check of the wire in the long axis, or a check of the wire in the short axis.
Then, the doctor checks if the wire is in good position.
If the wire is not in the good position, the doctor goes back to the puncture step.
If the wire is in the good position, the pathway is widen, the catheter is advanced, and the guirewire is removed.
Finally, the doctor verifies the flow and the reflow, and the catheter position is checked.

The doctor cleans the puncture area, and drapes the puncture zone.
The doctor configures the ultrasound, and puts gel in the probe.
Then, the doctor covers the probe and puts the sterile gel.
The doctor positions the probe and positions the patient.

The patient is anesthetize and punctured.
The blood return is checked.
If the blood return is not correct, the doctor goes back to the puncture step.
If the blood return is correct, the probe is dropped and the syringe is removed.
The guidewire is installed, and the trocar is removed.
Then the wire is checked using a check of the wire in the long axis, or a check of the wire in the short axis.
Then, the doctor checks if the wire is in good position.
If the wire is not in the good position, the doctor goes back to the puncture step.
If the wire is in the good position, the pathway is widen, the catheter is advanced, and the guirewire is removed.
Finally, the doctor verifies the flow and the reflow, and the catheter position is checked.

args.text: When a process description states that one or more unsuccessful checks cause the process to return to an earlier activity, model the repeated route with an exclusive gateway that merges the initial route and the return flows before that activity.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already covers modeling return loops and merging their routes before the repeated activity.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Give the outgoing sequence flows of an event-based gateway no conditionExpression; the first occurring target event selects the path.

args.text: When a process description states that multiple conditional failure paths return to the same earlier activity, and the initial route also proceeds to that activity, model the alternative routes as converging through an exclusive gateway before the activity.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers merging initial and retry paths before a repeated activity.

result.rule: When the description says that one of several alternatives is selected, or that an activity may occur: Model the choice or optional activity with an appropriate gateway, and reconnect the resulting paths before subsequent common work.

When the description says that work can branch into parallel or conditional activities, or that a setback returns the process to earlier work: Connect the affected activities with sequence flows, using gateways to represent the described branching or synchronization and preserving any stated return flow.

When the description states distinct activities leading to a decision, with one outcome returning work for another attempt and another outcome continuing the process.: Model the stated activities in their described order, then use a decision gateway to connect each outcome to its corresponding return or continuation path.

When the description says an optional activity may occur after a case reaches its completion, regardless of which outcome completed the case: Model the optional activity as a subsequent activity reached from the applicable completion paths, rather than as a new process start event.

args.text: When the description states that one or more conditional outcomes send work back to an earlier activity, and the normal route also reaches that activity: Model the normal route and the return flows as converging through an exclusive gateway immediately before the repeated activity.
